sentences.text: Gwalior, Dated: 15.3.2022  Shri Vivek Jain, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Pramod Pachauri, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.

This revision has been filed by the petitioner being aggrieved by the judgment passed by the First Additional Sessions Judge, Sabalgarh, Distt. Morena, in Criminal Appeal No.40/2017, whereby the appeal filed by the applicant against the judgment dated 2.2.2017 passed by the JMFC, Sabalgarh, in Criminal Case No.1001/2006 has been rejected.

entities.text: First Additional Sessions Judge, Sabalgarh, Distt. Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case necessary for disposal of this revision petition are that Complainant-Food Inspector, Food & Drugs Administration, Distt. Morena, filed a complaint against the applicant on the allegation that he took a sample of milk from Tanker No.MP06 E 1482 on 8.10.2002.
The applicant was accompanying the said vehicle in which mixed milk was being transported.
Aforesaid sample of the milk was sent to public analyst for his opinion.

Report of the public analyst came to the effect that aforesaid sample of the mixed milk does not conform to the standards inasmuch as though the amount of fat was found to be sufficient at 5.5% , but the amount of "solids not fat" was found to be at lower end at 7.365% in place of 8.5%.
Report of the public analyst was supplied to the applicant/accused.
Thereafter charge was framed and evidence was recorded by the trial Magistrate.

After conclusion of trial, applicant was convicted for the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as "the Act") vide judgment dated 2.2.2017.
Aggrieved by the conviction and sentence, applicant preferred an appeal before the Court of Session, which after hearing of above appeal, dismissed the same.
This revision petition has been filed on the ground that applicant was held guilty for the offence under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Act.

As per the report of the public analyst, in the sample "milk solids not fat"
was found below the prescribed standards.
In these situation, case of the applicant will fall under Section 2(ia)(m) wherein lesser punishment is prescribed.

It is further Vijay Singh Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94110936/
1 submitted that compliance of mandatory provisions of Section 13(2) of the Act is not done.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State supported the impugned judgment.
In the present scenario, it is to be examined as to whether Courts below have committed aforesaid illegality or not ?
On going through the report of the public analyst, it is emerged that sample of mixed milk was sent.
As per the report, milk fact is 5.5% and milk solids not fat is 7.365%.

Test for formalin was found positive, test for starch was found negative and test for added urea /fertilizer/detergent was found negative and BR reading at 40 degree Celsius (of extracted fact) was found to be 409.

As per opinion of public analyst,
sample does not conform as per the standards laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

As per argument of learned counsel for the petitioner, as only solids not fat was found to be on lower side at 7.365% in place of 8.5%, case of the applicant will fall under Section 2(ia)(m) wherein lesser punishment is prescribed.

It is true that case of the applicant falls under the definition of Section 2(ia)(m) which reads as under :-
"2. Definition.-In this Act unless the context otherwise requires,-
(ia) "adulterated"- an article of food shall be deemed to be adulterated- (a) to (l)....
(m) if the quality or purity of the article falls below the prescribed standard or its constitutes are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability but which does not render it injuries to health."
however, in the opinion of this Court, as per definition of adulterated given in 2(ia)m, this also comes under adulteration.
Beside this, as per the report of the chemical analyst, sample of the mixed milk does not conform to the standards.

As far as compliance of Section 13(2) is concerned, on going through the record of the trial Court and evidence of Food Inspector Rameshchandra Sharma (PW-1), it is abundantly clear that on receipt of the report of report of chemical analyst (Ex.P/11) notice under Section 13(2) of the Act was given to the applicant by Deputy Director Food and Drug Administration, Morena, which is Ex.P/14.
Receipt dated 21.2.2003 of sending the same by registered post is enclosed in the record.
Deputy Director Food and Drug Administration, Morena, after receiving the report of public analyst, gave permission to prosecute the present applicant under the aforesaid offence.

During evidence, Food Inspector Rameshchandra Sharma (PW-1) has categorically stated that along with chemical report,
he has sent information to the applicant/accused.
During cross-examination, in this regard defence could not carve out any discrepancy.

Beside this, his evidence is well supported by aforesaid Vijay Singh Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94110936/
2 documents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court in the case of Duli Chand Vs. Delhi Administration as reported in (1975) 4 SCC 649 has held that the jurisdiction of the High Court in a criminal revision application is severely restricted and it cannot embark upon a re-appreciation of evidence.

entities.text: Duli Chand Vs. Delhi Administration as reported in (1975) 4 SCC 649
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said judgment has been followed by the Apex Court in the case of State of Maharashtra Vs. Jagmohan Singh Kuldip Singh Anand and Others as reported in (2004) 7 SCC 659.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra Vs. Jagmohan Singh Kuldip Singh Anand and Others as reported in (2004) 7 SCC 659
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid, in the considered opinion of this Court, the Courts below have not committed any illegality in convicting and sentencing the applicant for the aforesaid offence, hence,
by affirming the impugned orders, this revision petition is dismissed.

(Deepak Kumar Agarwal) Judge ms/-
